answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce, nontransferable stake before voting on reputation or receiving valuable work. If peers verify fraud through audits, the dishonest identity loses its deposit. A sybil attacker must fund every account, so multiplying a sparrow flock multiplies capital at risk, unlike creating free accounts. This raises the cost of crossing the canyon of cheap identities, though a wealthy attacker can still pay and colluding auditors weaken the horizon of protection.
